item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Matchsticks are arranged as shown in the figures.

[Image: Matchstick patterns labeled Figure 1, Figure 2, and Figure 3]

If the pattern is continued, how many matchsticks would be used to make Figure 10?
item.figure_description:
Three figures formed by matchsticks arranged horizontally in a line, each ending with a triangular point pointing to the right:
- Figure 1: 1 square (4 matchsticks) with a triangle pointing right attached to the square's right vertical side (2 matchsticks), totaling 6 matchsticks.
- Figure 2: A row of 2 adjacent squares sharing an interior vertical matchstick (7 matchsticks) plus a triangle pointing right attached to the right side (2 matchsticks), totaling 9 matchsticks.
- Figure 3: A row of 3 adjacent squares sharing interior vertical matchsticks (10 matchsticks) plus a triangle pointing right attached to the right side (2 matchsticks), totaling 12 matchsticks.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three geometric figures composed of small congruent right triangles:
- Figure 1: A single square with a diagonal line from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner, dividing it into two right triangles labeled '1' (top-left) and '2' (bottom-right). Below the square is the label 'Figure 1'.
- Figure 2: A square divided into a 2-by-2 grid of 4 smaller squares. Each smaller square has a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 8 congruent triangles numbered 1 through 8: top-left square has 1 (upper) and 2 (lower); top-right square has 3 (upper) and 4 (lower); bottom-left square has 5 (upper) and 6 (lower); bottom-right square has 7 (upper) and 8 (lower). Below is the label 'Figure 2'.
- Figure 3: A square divided into a 3-by-3 grid of 9 smaller squares. Each smaller square has a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 18 congruent triangles. None of the triangles are numbered. Below is the label 'Figure 3'.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Two of the triangles below are similar.

[Image: Four triangles labeled I, II, III, IV]

Which two triangles are similar?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four triangles displayed side by side:
- Triangle I: A scalene obtuse triangle with a horizontal base at the bottom. The top vertex is closer to the left, so the left side is shorter than the right side.
- Triangle II: An acute isosceles triangle with a horizontal top edge. The two longer sides point downward to meet at a sharp vertex at the bottom.
- Triangle III: A tall, thin obtuse triangle with a short horizontal base at the bottom. The left side slants steeply upward to a top vertex, which connects via a long hypotenuse-like side down to the right end of the base.
- Triangle IV: A scalene obtuse triangle with a horizontal top edge, pointing downward to a vertex at the bottom offset to the right. It has the same shape and internal angles as Triangle I, but rotated 180° and reduced in size.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
